newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Saturday sought continued Chinese assistance for Bangladesh, particularly in infrastructure development.
The Dhaka City Corporation has ordered removal of all illegal structures from the city's roads, pavements, drains and parks by May 15.
Bangladesh was without electricity for about 30 minutes during mid-day on Saturday following the explosion of a transformer in Ashuganj power plant near Dhaka.
The driver of the Indian High Commissioner in Dhaka, Ram Pal, died on Saturday after taking alcohol.
A forum of small share investors has demanded special tribunal to try the 32 stock brokers and issuers allegedly involved in share price manipulation.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria on Saturday said the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) would be restructured and strengthened.
Cairn Energy of Britain, which struck gas in the Bay of Bengal, has formed alliance with the Dutch-British petroleum giant Shell Exploration for joint operations in Bangladesh.
Opposition leader and former Prime Minister, Begum Khaleda Zia, on Saturday accused the government of making Bangladesh "a vassal state" jeopardising its economy and sovereignty.
